details: The npm package pino-ulid claims to be a universally-unique, lexicographically-sortable identifier (ULID) generator, but is in fact a remote-access trojan. Its package.json postinstall script runs `node dist/node/utils.js` automatically on install (guarded by an existsSync check on the bundled dist files). dist/node/utils.js writes a PID lock file, registers OS persistence on Windows via schtasks and reg under the task/unit name `pkg-agent`, skips machines with fewer than 4 CPUs, and then launches dist/node/payload.js as a DETACHED child process. dist/node/payload.js (approx. 456 KB, SHA-256 3a9089e9db3650dd6d1584fae709022002dc34854b961abfb014a90f0a7c6a50) is the agent: it connects to a hardcoded WebSocket command-and-control (C2) server whose URL is obfuscated in dist/agent/config.js as a base64 string XORed with the 8-byte key [90,60,126,18,159,75,109,138], decoding to ws://95.216.232.162:8010/ (HTTP variant http://95.216.232.162:8010/, 15000 ms heartbeat). The agent registers with the C2 (sending a machine id and system info), reconnects on drop, and implements a `deploy_binary` command: the C2 sends base64 content that the agent writes to disk and executes, replacing the running agent and re-registering persistence. This gives the operator arbitrary remote code execution on the victim host. The ULID name and description are cover for the bundled auto-running remote-access agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code

files.note: Postinstall loader: registers Windows persistence (schtasks/reg as pkg-agent) and spawns dist/node/payload.js detached.
WebSocket C2 agent; deploy_binary command writes and runs attacker-supplied code (RCE).
